title: Chapter 8: Black Friday
html:
“Xiao San, this is a perfect chance to brush up on traditional Chinese architecture. This is an almost perfect reconstruction of a traditional Siheyuan 1 . Look at the layout: Dao Zuo Wu 2 , the Main House, the Ear Houses 3 , Chao Shou Corridor 4 , Chui Hua Men 5 , the East and West Houses, the Back House, Ru Yi Door 6 , and so on. The attention to detail is impressive; it really feels as though we’ve stepped back in time.” Gao Ru Xue moved through the set, occasionally stopping to study the construction.

“Senior, we’re in a Haunted House, not on a study trip. Do you mind?” Their footsteps echoed through the empty courtyard while paper money fluttered around them. He San and Gao Ru Xue might as well have been in different worlds. Every few seconds, he glanced over his shoulder, afraid something would leap from a dark corner. “We should find the exit as quickly as possible. This place is making me jumpy.”

“We’re already here, so we might as well enjoy the experience. Remember, we’re the customers. Don’t let the Haunted House control the pace.”

“But the boss said we have to find the exit within fifteen minutes. Judging by that wicked look on his face, I’m sure he has something nasty planned if we fail!” He San tried to hurry Gao Ru Xue along, but she remained completely unbothered.

“There are only so many tricks a Haunted House can use. At worst, an employee dressed as a ghost will chase us around. Xiao San, you study the dead every day. Don’t tell me you’ve suddenly become afraid of ghosts.” As Gao Ru Xue walked along the Chao Shou Corridor, she pushed open the door to the Left Ear House.

The Minghun set was modeled after an old Beijing Siheyuan. The Main House was traditionally occupied by the head of the household and the elders; the East and West Houses belonged to the sons and daughters, while the Ear Houses were used by servants.

When the door swung open, overturned tables and chairs came into view. The bed pillows had been torn apart, leaving cotton stuffing scattered across the floor, and a strip of white cloth swayed in the center of the room.

“Senior, I’ll watch the door. Be careful in there…” Before He San could finish, Gao Ru Xue dragged him into the room. He froze, his face going pale as he watched the white cloth move in the windless air.

“Interesting. The overturned furniture and signs of struggle make it look as though the Haunted House is staging a suspicious death rather than a simple haunting. But the Ear Houses were meant for servants, which suggests the specter’s anger extends even to people who had nothing to do with what happened to her.” Beneath Gao Ru Xue’s calm analysis was a hint of excitement. “This place is better designed than I expected. There may be more secrets hidden here.”

She circled the room and yanked away the faded bedcover. A paper doll lay underneath.

“A paper doll in a living person’s bed?” Gao Ru Xue tossed it aside and bent down to flip the mattress. There was nothing beneath it.

“The greater the expectation, the greater the disappointment… Looks like I overestimated this Haunted House. Let’s go. The exit isn’t here.” She shrugged and headed out. He San, left alone in the room, stood with his teeth chattering. Perhaps it was only the angle, but he could have sworn the paper doll on the floor winked at him.

“Bronze bird statues were said to weep blood, and the paper dolls offered to the dead were seen blinking… Senior, wait for me!”

As the Ear House door closed, the white cloth inside stopped swaying.

“Can you be a little quieter? Why are you screaming at everything? Pull yourself together.” Gao Ru Xue rolled her eyes while she waited for He San to catch up.

“I’m not scared, but this place makes me seriously uncomfortable, and the longer we stay, the stronger the feeling gets. Don’t you feel as though something is amplifying whatever we fear most?”

He San’s words struck a nerve. Gao Ru Xue thought about it and realized something did feel wrong. One of the most important qualities in forensic work was the ability to remain calm under pressure, yet when she had scolded He San earlier, her composure had slipped. That was unusual for her.

“Am I actually getting scared too? But why? Everything here is obviously fake.” A crack appeared in Gao Ru Xue’s mental defenses. Neither of them understood where the fear was coming from. Suspicion and psychological pressure fed each other, allowing the first seed of fear to take root.

“Do you think something might actually be living here? The boss did say the building stands on an old burial ground and used to be part of an abandoned hospital…”

“Shush! Our university’s anatomy lab is creepier than this. You study forensics—how are you this easily frightened?” Despite insisting she was not afraid, Gao Ru Xue was noticeably speaking faster. She scanned the old house, mourning hall, dead trees, and fluttering paper money. They were all props. None of them should have been frightening. “Then what am I afraid of?”

The two were so focused on their surroundings that neither paid attention to the background music looping around them. Black Friday had slowly worked its way into their awareness, deepening the unease already taking hold.

“Xiao San, how long have we been in here already?”

“I have no idea, but I have a feeling we won’t be able to escape in fifteen minutes!”

“Don’t panic. Give me a moment to think.” Gao Ru Xue continued down the corridor. “This Haunted House isn’t actually that frightening. The owner has been planting negative suggestions in our minds from the moment we entered—burial grounds, premature death, ghosts, all of it. It’s a classic way of making visitors more vulnerable to fear. The cleverest part is the time limit. He told us we have fifteen minutes but never said what happens if we fail, so our own minds fill in the blank with the worst possibility.”

“Then what should we do? This Haunted House does feel different from the others.” He San was straightforward by nature; he usually followed whatever his senior told him to do.

“You’re right about that. An ordinary Haunted House relies on actors dressed as ghosts or elaborate props to create shocking scenes, but this one doesn’t. The set was prepared in advance and we’re allowed to explore freely. Without a guide or a fixed sequence, we never know what will happen next.”

“I get it. The unknown is the scariest part.” He San nodded.

“That explanation is as good as any.” Gao Ru Xue frowned slightly. “Come on. Let’s move on to the next room.”

The Ear House connected directly to the Main House. Gao Ru Xue pushed open another wooden door and found a room filled with mourning clothes, with a painted coffin positioned in the center.

A large white-paper “喜” character had been pasted onto the red coffin. Rows of paper mannequins stood neatly on either side.

Each mannequin had a name written on its back and a thin layer of makeup painted across its face. When the door opened, their eyes seemed to gleam, as though all of them were silently watching the two people at the entrance.
